_note: Human grading rubric for Stylist eval answers. Score each dimension 0 / 1 / 2, or N/A when it doesn't apply (e.g. product fit on a decline). The verdict is derived: Pass when no critical dimension scores 0 and the total is at least passPct of the applicable maximum. Use the question's must / must-not lines as the answer key.

dimensions.name: Understood the ask
dimensions.help: Did it read the intent and pick the right move: search, check policy, ask one question, or decline?

levels.2: Right intent and right move; picked up occasion, budget, who it's for, Hinglish/typos
levels.1: Mostly right, but missed or misread one part of the ask
levels.0: Wrong move (searched when it should decline or ask) or misread the request

dimensions.name: Respected constraints
dimensions.help: Price, size, gender, returns, brand exclusions: kept, or clearly flagged when relaxed.

levels.2: Every hard limit kept, or any relaxation stated plainly ("₹400 over budget")
levels.1: A minor slip, or a relaxation that was only vaguely flagged
levels.0: Broke a limit silently (over budget, wrong gender, non-returnable when asked)

dimensions.name: Product fit
dimensions.help: Would you actually show these pieces to a friend for this ask? N/A if no products were expected.

levels.2: Strong picks for the occasion, fabric and style; at least 3 good options
levels.1: Some good picks mixed with weak or generic ones
levels.0: Mostly irrelevant (wrong category, wrong occasion, accessories for clothing)

dimensions.name: Accurate & grounded
dimensions.help: Only claims the tools support: real products, real prices, policy lines quoted correctly, no invented facts.

levels.2: Everything checks out; uncertainty is admitted ("not clearly stated")
levels.1: A small overstatement or imprecise detail, nothing misleading
levels.0: Invented a product, price, policy or fact, or stated something false

dimensions.name: Helpful & clear
dimensions.help: Concise, warm, explains why the picks fit, gives a useful next step.

levels.2: Short, clear, explains the why; you'd be happy if a shopper saw it
levels.1: Fine but generic, too long, or missing the why
